## Unlock scan: `pm:blocked` → `pm:queue`, premise re-verified

`domain:services` execution seat, session `session_01AUF1NoViznQK32gqpK8wS8`. Label write was read-modify-write with the read immediately before it, comparative read-back against `union(current, target)` = `{tooling, domain:services, priority:p3, pm:queue}` — matched.

**Blocker satisfied:** the comment-channel `Blocked-by: #14062` (comment 5502968282) is discharged — #14062 closed `completed` at 2026-09-02T06:45:01Z.

**Premise re-verified on the merged ref, and it holds** — the class fix for #14062 did not incidentally cover this instance:

```
git ls-tree origin/main packages/services/service-cluster/ | grep tsconfig
  →  packages/services/service-cluster/tsconfig.json     (ONLY — no tsconfig.test.json)

git ls-tree -r origin/main --name-only packages/services/service-cluster/ | grep memory.contract.test
  →  packages/services/service-cluster/src/memory/memory.contract.test.ts   (present)
```

⇒ `service-cluster` still has no test-layer tsc program, so its test files — including `memory.contract.test.ts`, the package's contract witness — still compile under no program, and the TS2322 the card names is still unobserved by any gate. The card is not stale.

⛔ **Disclosure: this release is ~33 hours late and that is this seat's fault, not a tooling gap.** The `Blocked-by:` line parses and the H4/H19 patrol reads both the body and comment channels. That patrol is **report-only, exit code always 0** — *returning* a card is a seat action, and for a `domain:services` card that seat is this one. It had not run its unlock scan.

Not dispatched in this round: R23 already has an in-flight dev and the lane's p0 chain (#13566 / #14970 / #14971) takes precedence. Available to the next round as an ordinary `pm:queue` card.

## The route #14062 settled on, read off the tree rather than guessed

Triage's grading note (5502968282) made this card's shape conditional: *"the route is whatever #14062 settles on, adopted by wiring."* #14062 closed `completed` 2026-09-02T06:45:01Z with **no linked closing PR**, so the settlement is not readable from the issue — it is readable from what the plugin family now looks like on `origin/main`:

| package | tsconfigs present | `typecheck` script |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `plugin-sharing` | `tsconfig.json`, `tsconfig.scripts.json`, **`tsconfig.test.json`** | **yes** |
| `plugin-auth` | `tsconfig.json`, `tsconfig.examples.json`, **`tsconfig.test.json`** | **yes** |
| `plugin-webhooks` | `tsconfig.json`, `tsconfig.scripts.json`, **`tsconfig.test.json`** | **yes** |
| **`service-cluster`** | `tsconfig.json` **only** | **no** — scripts are `build`, `test` |

⇒ The settled route is the **checked test zone**: a `tsconfig.test.json` plus a `typecheck` script, adopted by wiring. Not "deliberate exclusion with pins re-sited", which was the other branch the card named. The three exemplars above are the shape to copy — ⛔ copy the one that fits this package, do not invent a fourth spelling.

## Premise re-verified on the merged ref

Already measured by this seat when the card was released from `pm:blocked` (comment 5528349064): `service-cluster` still has no test-layer program, and `src/memory/memory.contract.test.ts` is still present. The #14062 class fix did **not** incidentally cover this instance.

## ⚠️ The scope risk this dispatch exists to fence

#14062's own title records that **`plugin-approvals` alone hid 345 type errors** once a program was pointed at its tests. This card's measurement names exactly one error in `service-cluster` (a `TS2322` in the contract witness at `memory.contract.test.ts:26`), but that was a one-off `tsc --noEmit` at worktree `44a2e59b` — **it is not a promise about today's count**, and turning the program on is what discovers the real number.

Two hard constraints make "just work through them" the wrong default:

- ⛔ **`test-typecheck-debt.json` is shrink-only and maintainer-only (#5286).** The dev may not grow it. Triage was explicit: the measured `TS2322` *"is to be fixed, not ledgered."*
- This is a **p3**. A card that turns into a hundred hand-fixed type errors is no longer a p3 and should not be finished on that basis.

⇒ **Falsifier, and it is the most likely outcome worth catching:** measure the error count first, before fixing anything. If enabling the program surfaces more than a handful, **stop and report the count and a representative sample** — do not ledger them (forbidden), do not grind through them, and do not narrow the program to hide them. That report is a good result and re-scopes the card; it is not a failure.

Size S, `opus`.

## A live, dated instance of what this gap costs — measured today on PR #14994

`domain:services` execution seat, session `session_01AUF1NoViznQK32gqpK8wS8`. Recording evidence, ⛔ not re-grading the card and ⛔ not widening the dispatched scope (still `service-cluster` alone).

This card exists so `packages/services/**` is *in the population* when #14062's class decision is applied. Today an unrelated PR in this lane demonstrated the harm concretely, which is worth more than the argument for it.

**PR #14994** (card #14328) added a test file to `@objectstack/service-automation` containing a `… as never` cast that erased a contextual type, leaving a callback parameter implicitly `any` — a plain **TS7006**. What happened to it:

| where it should have been caught | what happened |
|:--|:--|
| the dev's local run | invisible — the package has **no `typecheck` script**, so there was nothing to run |
| `Type Check · workspace` | **passed** |
| `Type Check · source gates` | **passed** |
| `Type Check · consumer gates` | **passed** |
| `Type Check · debt ledger` | **FAILED** — the only lane that saw it |

And the way it surfaced is the part that matters: the debt lane compiles `src/**` (tests included) and is a **shrink-only ratchet**, so a newly-written untyped test does not report as *"you wrote an untyped test."* It reports as:

> `@objectstack/service-automation: DEBT records 3 raw tsc error(s), tsc --noEmit now reports 4 (+1). DEBT is frozen debt, not a permission slip`

⇒ **The author's own new error arrives disguised as ledger drift**, in a gate whose remedy text is mostly about not raising the entry. That is a materially worse failure mode than a plain type error in a package `typecheck`, and it is the mode every package in this family is in.

The fix in that PR was correct and cost a full CI cycle: type the double as the real `FlowTrigger` instead of casting it away (`4dd73b545`). ⛔ Nothing was ledgered.

## The family, measured just now on `origin/main`

Of **16** packages under `packages/services/`, **4** have no `typecheck` script:

```
service-automation   service-cluster   service-knowledge   service-storage
```

(Control: 16 packages actually read — an earlier pass of mine returned "0 missing" from a broken path join and I discarded it; a zero with no control is not a reading.)

So this card's `service-cluster` is **one of four**, not the whole services instance. ⛔ I am **not** filing the other three as cards — #14062 set the family-per-card pattern and the class decision governs all of them; naming them here is so whoever applies that decision knows the real size, and so the dispatched `service-cluster` round is not mistaken for closing the family.

⚠️ Note for the in-flight `service-cluster` round: `service-automation`'s errors are **ledgered** (3 frozen), while `service-cluster`'s are not ledgered at all — so pointing a program at `service-cluster` may surface a count that has never been recorded anywhere. That is the scope risk the dispatch already fenced with stop-and-report, and this measurement makes it more likely, not less.

## ⛔ Correction to my comment above (5529278535) — the ledger claim was wrong

`domain:services` execution seat. That comment ended with:

> ⚠️ Note for the in-flight `service-cluster` round: `service-automation`'s errors are **ledgered** (3 frozen), while `service-cluster`'s are **not ledgered at all** — so pointing a program at `service-cluster` may surface a count that has never been recorded anywhere.

**The second half is false.** `service-cluster` *did* carry a ledger entry, and it recorded exactly the error this card names. Verified at the tree, on the base the dispatched round actually built from:

```
44ffa2103  scripts/check-type-check-coverage.mjs:693
  '@objectstack/service-cluster': { errors: 1, note: 'code-tier 1 (TS2322).' },
```

**How I got it wrong:** I inferred it from the package having no `typecheck` script, and never measured it. Having no script and having no ledger entry are different facts — the DEBT ledger exists precisely to carry packages that no script reaches, so the absence of one is not evidence of the other. It was an assumption stated as a measurement, in a comment whose whole point was to supply measurements.

The dev on PR #15032 caught it and corrected me rather than building on it, which is the right call and the reason it cost nothing.

### Two consequences, both good rather than bad

1. **The scope risk I flagged did not materialise, and the ledger is why.** I warned that `service-cluster` might surface "a number nobody has ever recorded." The number was **1**, and it was recorded — the ledger's `errors: 1` matched the measurement exactly. My stop-and-report valve was never triggered.
2. **Deleting that entry was required, not scope creep.** The coverage gate fails a package that declares `typecheck` while still sitting in DEBT, so the graduation had to land in the same PR. Anyone reading #15032's diff should read the ledger deletion as the card completing, not as an unrelated edit.

The rest of that comment stands as measured: the PR #14994 instance (a TS7006 invisible to three of four type-check lanes and surfacing only in the shrink-only debt ratchet, disguised as ledger drift) is unaffected, as is the family count — 4 of 16 `packages/services/*` lack a `typecheck` script. With #15032 that becomes 3: `service-automation` (DEBT 3), `service-knowledge` (DEBT 10), `service-storage` (DEBT 51) — all three tracked in DEBT, none invisible, each wanting its own card under the #14062 family-per-card pattern.

## Family scheduled — the three siblings are now carded

`domain:services` execution seat. This card's dev reported three remaining `packages/services/*` packages with no `typecheck` script and correctly did **not** touch them (family-per-card, per #14062). Scheduling them was this seat's, and it is done:

- **#15048** — `service-automation` (DEBT 3). ⭐ The package where PR #14994's TS7006 incident actually happened, so its evidence is first-hand.
- **#15049** — `service-knowledge` (DEBT 10).
- **#15050** — `service-storage` (DEBT 51). Largest, and the most likely to trip the stop-and-report valve.

Each carries the settled route, the two non-obvious findings this card produced (copy the exemplar whose **build** config does not exclude tests — `plugin-auth`/`plugin-sharing`/`core` do, and AGENTS.md forbids adding such an exclusion; and the package's DEBT entry must be deleted in the same PR), the measure-both-ways instruction with the `core` 98→4 vs `service-cluster` 1→1 contrast, and the `check:type-source-resolution` re-baseline ruling from PR #15032. ⛔ All three filed without `domain:*`, type or priority — those are triage's.

With `service-cluster` graduating, the services family goes 4 → 3.
